scope: Independent read-only inspection of listed actual Godot PNGs and chronological frame samples. No engine run or synthesized images.
observations: Before-contact side has a lower muzzle and narrower jaw opening. Full-depth stab and twist side/front views clearly show the muzzle tilted upward and the lower jaw opened into a scream-like pose.

The visible tongue remains inside the mouth; no detached floating tongue or gross upper/lower tooth interpenetration is apparent in these views. This is visual inspection, not exact mouth mesh collision analysis.
Head and neck silhouette remain connected. Small stretched/folded areas under the side skin flaps are visible, but no open neck seam or detached head is apparent.

First-person rear view reveals a rising head/muzzle silhouette above the upper back. The mouth itself is naturally occluded from this camera and should not be described as clearly visible in first person.
Chronological 1.33/1.40/1.47-second samples show the head rising with penetration. 2.60/2.73/2.87-second samples show the held pose passing into collapse without an obvious isolated head snap.
The initial upward head reaction is visually stronger than the additional twist pulse. Blood and sword grip remain visible.
limitations: Only listed stills and sample frames were independently inspected; full real-time playback and hardware input were not exercised.
The pose communicates a scream visually, but this review did not verify or hear an audio scream.
Original model skin topology, sleeve and finger art limitations were not newly solved by this change.
conclusion: No observed blocker in upward-head/lower-jaw direction, visible neck connection or sampled transition. Front/side images give stronger evidence than the rear first-person view.
